title: Taking away by counting back
examples: How do I subtract on a number line?

explain.say: You have 15 grapes. You eat 6 of them. How many are left? Look at the number line. You start at 15. This time you hop backwards.
Put your finger on 15. That is how many grapes you start with. Taking away makes the number smaller. So you hop to the left.
Hop back 5 times: 14, 13, 12, 11, 10. 15 take away 5 is 10. You ate 6 grapes, so you need 1 more hop.
1 more hop takes you to 9. So 15 take away 6 equals 9. You ate 6 grapes, and 9 are left. Check it by hopping forward 6 from 9.
Hopping back to 10 first is the same make-ten idea you use to add. Look at 13 take away 4. Hop back 3 to 10. Hop back 1 more to 9. Now try 16 take away 7.

faq.a: Counting back means starting at a number and counting down. For 15 take away 6, you count 14, 13, 12, 11, 10, 9.

faq.q: How do I subtract on a number line?
faq.a: Put your finger on the first number and hop left once for each number you take away. Where you land is the answer.
asks: How do I take away on a number line?

faq.a: 15 take away 6 is 9. Count back 6 hops from 15: 14, 13, 12, 11, 10, 9.

faq.q: Why do I hop to the left?
faq.a: On a number line, numbers get smaller as you go left. Taking away makes a number smaller, so you move left.

faq.q: How can I check a take-away sum?
faq.a: Hop forward again. 9 plus 6 brings you back to 15, so 15 take away 6 must be 9.

facts: Subtraction can be shown as hops to the left on a number line.

quiz.say: Start at 12. Hop back 4. Where do you land?
quiz.show: Start at 12. Hop back 4. Where do you land?
quiz.why: Hop back from 12: 11, 10, 9, 8. 4 hops back land on 8.

wrong.1: 9 counts 12 as the first hop. Your first hop goes from 12 to 11.
wrong.2: 16 is 4 hops forward. Taking away hops back.

quiz.say: Find 14 take away 5 on a number line. Which way works?
quiz.why: From 14, back 4 is 10. Back 1 more is 9, so that is 5 hops back.

wrong.2: Start at 14, the number you take away from.
